record.summary: Priya Menon bought a 55‑inch smart TV for Rs 62,000 from an online marketplace during a festival sale. The listing promised a 1‑year brand warranty and a 7‑day replacement. The TV arrived with a dented box but worked initially. After 19 days a vertical line appeared on the screen (day 20) and a week later the panel failed completely (day 27). She lodged a complaint on the platform; the seller claimed the damage was physical and outside the 7‑day window, while the brand’s service centre technician marked the issue as "customer damage, warranty void" without opening the TV. Over the next six weeks she dealt with calls and chats, receiving conflicting replies from the seller, the brand and the platform. She now seeks a refund or replacement and compensation for the harassment, and wants to know who is legally responsible and which forum to approach.
record.goal: Obtain a refund or replacement of the TV and compensation for the harassment; determine the legally responsible party and appropriate forum for redress.
questions: On what exact date (or approximate date) did you place the order and receive the TV?
In which city and state did the delivery take place (your current location)?
Do you have any written response (email or letter) from the seller or the platform stating their position on the warranty or replacement?
Have you attempted to register the warranty on the brand’s website, and if so, what result did you receive?
Can you provide a brief timeline (dates) of the six weeks of calls and chats, or any logs that show when each communication occurred?
contradictions: Seller says the 7‑day replacement window has lapsed, while the defect appeared after 19 days.
Brand’s technician declares the damage "physical" and warranty void, yet there is no evidence of impact marks or mishandling.
Platform claims it is only an intermediary, yet its chat transcript indicates the seller will resolve the issue.
evidence: Order invoice showing purchase price and date.
Product listing screenshot displaying "1‑year brand warranty + 7‑day replacement".
Unboxing video showing dented box and working screen on delivery day.
Photos of the screen with the vertical line and later the complete failure, with matching file timestamps.
Chat transcripts and email threads with the platform, seller and brand indicating the back‑and‑forth communication.
Technician's service report stating "physical damage suspected, warranty void" without photographs or inspection details.
Missing warranty card from the box; brand website claim that warranty registers automatically on purchase.
Courier handover photo showing the box being carried loosely.

suggestions.title: Purchase, promised terms and communications
suggestions.look_for: Look for the order confirmation, invoice, payment record and relevant warranty or service terms. Keep the complete email or chat thread.
suggestions.why: These can show what was purchased, what was promised and what resolution the seller offered.
suggestions.action: Keep the original files or exports. Record dates and ask for copies from the seller or platform if you do not have them.

suggestions.title: Condition of the product or work
suggestions.look_for: If safe, note the model or order number, the fault and when it appeared. Keep existing dated photos, service requests or repair reports.
suggestions.why: A dated record helps distinguish what you observed from a possible explanation of the fault.
suggestions.action: Leave suspected electrical or other hazardous damage to a qualified person. Ask the repair provider for a written report if they inspect it.

suggestions.title: Original records and an evidence log
suggestions.look_for: Keep records you lawfully have, with their surrounding context. For each item note the related event, who provided it, when you received it, and any transfer.
suggestions.why: The log distinguishes what you observed from what someone later told you and makes it easier to check the source.
suggestions.action: Keep an unchanged original and label working copies. Avoid editing originals, guessing gaps, or sharing evidence publicly.
